name: PCB Reverse Engineering & Schematic Reconstruction
description: Systematic analysis of printed circuit boards to identify components, trace connectivity, and reconstruct schematics. Covers component identification (IC marking decoding, package identification), net tracing on multi-layer PCBs, X-ray imaging for hidden traces and BGA connections, test point identification, and schematic capture for attack surface mapping.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to PCB reverse engineering

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands PCB construction, component types, and the purpose of board-level reverse engineering
evidence: Can identify common PCB component types (MCU, flash, PMIC, passives, connectors)
Understands multi-layer PCB construction (layer stackup, vias, ground planes)
Aware of common IC marking conventions and how to look up datasheets

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies components and traces basic signal paths on PCBs under supervision
evidence: Decodes IC markings and locates relevant datasheets and pinout information
Uses multimeter continuity testing to trace signal paths between components
Identifies power rails, clock signals, and common buses (SPI, I2C, UART) on a PCB with guidance
Documents identified components and connections following lab templates

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently reverse engineers PCBs and produces actionable schematics
evidence: Reconstructs partial or full schematics from multi-layer PCBs using X-ray and visual inspection
Identifies debug headers, test points, and unpopulated pads with security relevance
Maps complete communication bus topology and identifies interception points
Produced PCB RE reports with schematics on 3+ engagements meeting lab standards

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Reverse engineers complex boards; develops RE methodology; mentors team
evidence: Reverse engineers high-density boards (10+ layer, fine-pitch BGA) using X-ray tomography
Identifies and analyzes custom ASICs and undocumented components through pin analysis
Develops standardized PCB RE workflows and documentation templates for the lab
Mentors junior analysts on component identification and efficient RE techniques

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on PCB RE; defines methodology; specifies lab equipment
evidence: Defines the lab's PCB RE methodology and quality standards
Evaluates and specifies X-ray and inspection equipment for PCB analysis
Reverse engineers boards with intentional anti-RE measures (buried vias, potting, scraped markings)
Trains teams on PCB RE techniques and mentors across multiple engagement types

assessment_methods.description: Reverse engineer a prepared target PCB: identify all major components, reconstruct key signal paths, and produce a partial schematic with identified attack surfaces
Review PCB RE documentation and schematics from recent engagements for accuracy and completeness

equipment: X-ray inspection system (2D or CT) for PCB layer analysis
PCB cross-section polishing and microscopy system
